meaning: the entity has fields the knobs set: JSON pointers into its own components, each mapped to an integer expression over the knobs whose value replaces the default written there
_notes: `owner` is `agent-studio`, who answers for this shape today; the registry moves ownership freely (world-proto server/DESIGN.md section 7). Lead decided, say if not.

The schema is open to fields it does not name, as every registry schema is (world-proto SPEC section 9's lenient reading), so a misspelt optional field passes WPS and is carried unread. Lead decided, say if not.

The schema describes the value as bound: inside a piece the template evaluation engine replaces `$param` and `local_ref` before it validates this component (the instantiation step, 05-template-workflow.md section 3.6), so no field accepts either placeholder, and a top-level template entity holds none (section 3.4, rule 1). Lead decided, say if not.
Not in the schema, the template evaluation engine's to check: a pointer names an integer the entity holds at the default knobs, and never a reference field, which only the registry's annotations say.

schema.title: template.knob_binding
schema.description: the entity has fields the knobs set: JSON pointers into its own components, each mapped to an integer expression over the knobs whose value replaces the default written there
schema.$comment: Written for world-proto's registry from Agent Studio's 05-template-workflow.md section 3.2 (notes/agent-studio-2026-10-17/design/specs/05-template-workflow.md). Open to fields a newer writer adds (SPEC section 9).

pointer.title: binding pointer
pointer.description: A JSON pointer into the entity's own components (a piece internal's, inside a piece), its first segment the component: never `template.knob_binding`, `template.presence` or `external_ids`.

expression.title: knob expression
expression.description: An integer expression over the template's knobs: integers, knob keys, + - * / (floor division), min and max, parentheses, separated by spaces (05-template-workflow.md section 3.3). The schema holds its alphabet and its 512-character limit; the template evaluation engine parses it and refuses a name that is not a declared knob.
